Control your Google Cast devices from Gladys: Chromecast, Google Nest speakers
and displays (Nest Mini, Nest Audio, Nest Hub...), TVs with Chromecast built-in
or Google TV, and the speaker groups of the Google Home app.

Everything happens on your **local network**: no Google account, no cloud, no
API key. This integration replaces the Google Cast integration built into
Gladys, with much more than announcements.

## Where it works

- **Countries**: everywhere. Google Cast is a local protocol, with no regional
  service behind it: the integration works in every country and region where
  Cast devices are sold, whatever the language of the device.
- **Network**: Gladys and the Cast devices must share the same local network.
  Discovery uses mDNS (the same as your phone), which does not cross routers:
  a device on another VLAN or subnet can still be added by its IP address (see
  _Manual addresses_), as long as Gladys can reach it on TCP port 8009 (and
  32000-33000 for speaker groups).
- **From outside your home**: the Cast devices are only reachable from your
  home network, but Gladys is too — the dashboard, the scenes and Gladys Plus
  work from anywhere, Gladys relays the commands locally.

Requires Gladys Assistant **5.3.0 or later**.

## What you get

Each Cast device becomes a music player in Gladys, with:

- the **"now playing" card** on the dashboard: title, artist, album, artwork,
  progress, play / pause / previous / next, whatever app casts (Spotify,
  YouTube Music, Deezer, a web radio...);
- **volume** and **mute**, kept in sync when someone changes them from a
  phone or the device itself;
- **announcements**: the "Play a notification" scene action of Gladys speaks
  on the device (text-to-speech);
- a **local** badge on the device, red when the device is unreachable.

The integration keeps a connection open to each device you added: every
change is pushed by the device, nothing is polled.

## Installation and configuration

1. Install **Google Cast** from the integration catalog.
2. Open the **Discovery** tab: the Cast devices of your network are listed.
   Add the ones you want. The speaker groups appear too.
3. That's it. The **Configuration** tab offers a few options:
   - **Manual addresses**: the IP addresses of the devices the discovery does
     not find (another VLAN), separated by commas, e.g.
     `192.168.20.15, 192.168.20.16:8009`. Give these devices a fixed address
     in your router: the address identifies them.
   - **Speaker groups**: uncheck to hide the speaker groups.
   - **Announcement volume**: the volume of the Gladys announcements, from 1
     to 100 %; the previous volume comes back after the announcement. `0`
     keeps the current volume.
   - **Scan duration**: raise it if some devices are missing from the
     Discovery tab.

Buttons of the Configuration tab:

- **Search the network**: finds the devices again (new ones go to the
  Discovery tab) and refreshes the addresses of the known ones.
- **Test a device**: connects to the chosen device and shows its volume and
  the app it runs.

A device whose address changed (new DHCP lease) is found again automatically
after a few failed connections.

## Scenes

### Triggers

In the scene editor, under the integration's category:

- **Cast playback started**: something starts or resumes playing, or the
  track changes. Variables: `title`, `artist`, `app`.
- **Cast playback stopped**: the media ended, was stopped, interrupted or
  failed. Filter on the reason if you wish. Variables: `reason` (`finished`,
  `cancelled`, `interrupted`, `error`), `title`.
- **Cast app launched**: an app starts casting (YouTube, Netflix, Spotify...).
  Filter on its exact name if you wish. Variables: `app`, `app_id`.
- **Cast device online / offline**: a device became reachable or unreachable.
  Variable: `status` (`online`, `offline`).

Each trigger can be limited to one device; left empty, any device matches. The
variables are read with `{{triggerEvent.data.title}}` in the following
actions. What the integration casts itself (scene actions, announcements)
never fires these triggers, so a scene cannot loop.

The volume and the playback state are device features too: the standard
"Device state" trigger works on them ("when the TV is paused...").

### Actions

- **Cast a media**: plays a URL on a device: a web radio, a sound, a video, a
  picture (e.g. a camera snapshot). Pick the format, or let the integration
  guess it from the URL; tick _Live stream_ for a web radio. Output:
  `played`.
- **Play a sound**: plays a short sound (doorbell chime, alarm) at the chosen
  volume, then restores the previous volume. Output: `played`.
- **Stop casting**: quits the app casting to the device. Output: `stopped`
  (false when nothing was casting).
- **Launch a Cast app**: opens an app from its Cast app id, e.g. `233637DE`
  (YouTube). Output: `launched`.

The URL must be reachable by the Cast device itself (a public URL, or an
address of your local network). An unreachable device does not stop the
scene: the output is `false`, use it in a condition if needed.

The standard Gladys actions work too: **Play a notification**
(text-to-speech), **Set the value of a device** (volume, mute, playback
state).

## Dashboard

- The core **Music** card shows any Cast device, with its artwork and
  controls.
- **Google Cast devices** widget: every device at a glance (online, the app
  casting, what plays).
- **Google Cast player** widget: one device, its live volume, the artwork,
  the title and artist, and the play / pause, next and stop buttons.

## Migrating from the built-in Google Cast integration

The devices of this integration are new Gladys devices:

1. Add the devices from the Discovery tab of this integration.
2. In your scenes, point the **Play a notification** actions to the new
   devices, and update your dashboards.
3. Delete the devices of the built-in integration (Integrations → Google Cast
   → Devices).

## Troubleshooting

- **No device in the Discovery tab**: the devices must be on the same
  network as Gladys. Check that they show up in the Google Home app on the
  same Wi-Fi, raise the scan duration, or use the manual addresses.
- **Unreachable badge**: the device is off, or its address changed. Use
  **Search the network**, then **Test a device**.
- **No sound for the announcements**: the Cast device downloads the voice clip
  from Gladys: it must be able to reach the Gladys address on your network.
- **Nothing happens on next / previous**: some apps (YouTube, Netflix) do not
  accept these commands from another sender.

Logs: Integrations → Google Cast → Logs. Set the `LOG_LEVEL` environment
variable to `debug` for the full detail.

## Privacy and security

The integration only talks to the Cast devices of your local network
(encrypted TLS connection, port 8009) and, for the dashboard artwork, to the
image servers of the apps that cast. No data leaves your home otherwise.
See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Google-Cast/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
to report a vulnerability.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Google Cast asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Everything stays on your local network: no Google account, no cloud. Gladys finds your Cast devices (Chromecast, Google Nest, TVs with Chromecast built-in, speaker groups) by mDNS: open the Discovery tab and add them. Works in every country. |
| Manual addresses | `string` | No | Only for devices mDNS cannot reach (another VLAN or subnet): their IP addresses, separated by commas, with an optional :port. Give them a fixed address in your router. |
| Speaker groups | `boolean` | No | Also offer the speaker groups created in the Google Home app. |
| Announcement volume (%) | `number` | No | Volume of the Gladys announcements (text-to-speech), the previous volume coming back afterwards. 0 keeps the current volume. |
| Scan duration (s) | `number` | No | How long to listen for devices during a scan. Raise it if some devices are missing. |

## How to install Google Cast in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Google Cast appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/gboulvin/gladys-google-cast:1.0.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Google-Cast](https://github.com/gboulvin/Gladys-Google-Cast).

Google Cast requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Google Cast is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [gboulvin](https://github.com/gboulvin), not by the Gladys core team.
